1: 1 There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was whole-hearted and upright, and one that feared God, and shunned evil. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And his sons used to go and hold a feast in the house of each one upon his day; and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and to drink with them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt-offerings according to the number of them all; for Job said: 'It may be that my sons have sinned, and blasphemed God in their hearts.' Thus did Job continually. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Now it fell upon a day, that the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord , and Satan came also among them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And the Lord said unto Satan: 'Whence comest thou?' Then Satan answered the Lord , and said: 'From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And the Lord said unto Satan: 'Hast thou considered My servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a whole-hearted and an upright man, one that feareth God, and shunneth evil?' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Then Satan answered the Lord , and said: 'Doth Job fear God for nought? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Hast not Thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath, on every side? Thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions are increased in the land. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
But put forth Thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, surely he will blaspheme Thee to Thy face.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And the Lord said unto Satan: 'Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thy hand.' So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord . <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And it fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
that there came a messenger unto Job, and said: 'The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
and the Sabeans made a raid, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said: 'A fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said: 'The Chaldeans set themselves in three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have taken them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and  ​ I only am escaped alone to tell thee.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said: 'Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

and, behold, there came a great wind from across the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young people, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

and he said: Naked came I out of my mother's womb, And naked shall I return thither; The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; Blessed be the name of the Lord . <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
For all this Job sinned not, nor ascribed aught unseemly to God. <span class="anchor"
2: 2 Again it fell upon a day, that the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord , and Satan came also among them to present himself before the Lord . <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And the Lord said unto Satan: 'From whence comest thou?' And Satan answered the Lord , and said: 'From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And the Lord said unto Satan: 'Hast thou considered My servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a whole-hearted and an upright man, one that feareth God, and shunneth evil? and he still holdeth fast his integrity, although thou didst move Me against him, to destroy him without cause.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And Satan answered the Lord , and said: 'Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
But put forth Thy hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, surely he will blaspheme Thee to Thy face.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And the Lord said unto Satan: 'Behold, he is in thy hand; only spare his life.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord , and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot even unto his crown. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself therewith; and he sat among the ashes. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
Then said his wife unto him: 'Dost thou still hold fast thine integrity? blaspheme God, and die.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

But he said unto her: 'Thou speakest as one of the impious women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?' For all this did not Job sin with his lips. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to bemoan him and to comfort him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and threw dust upon their heads toward heaven. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word unto him; for they saw that his grief was very great. <span class="anchor"
3: 3 After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And Job spoke and said: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let the day perish wherein I was born, And the night wherein it was said: 'A man-child is brought forth.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let that day be darkness; Let not God inquire after it from above,  ​ Neither let the light shine upon it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own; Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let all that maketh black the day terrify it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
As for that night, let thick darkness seize upon it; Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; Let it not come into the number of the months. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lo, let that night be desolate; Let no joyful voice come therein. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let them curse it that curse the day, Who are ready to rouse up leviathan. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; Let it look for light, but have none; Neither let it behold the eyelids of the morning; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Because it shut not up the doors of my [mother's] womb, Nor hid trouble from mine eyes. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Why died I not from the womb? Why did I not perish at birth? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Why did the knees receive me? And wherefore the breasts, that I should suck? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For now should I have lain still and been quiet; I should have slept; then had I been at rest— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
With kings and counsellors of the earth, Who built up waste places for themselves; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Or with princes that had gold, Who filled their houses with silver; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been; As infants that never saw light. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
There the wicked cease from troubling; And there the weary are at rest. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
There the prisoners are at ease together; They hear not the voice of the taskmaster. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The small and great are there alike; And the servant is free from his master. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Wherewith is light given to him that is in misery, And life unto the bitter in soul— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who long for death, but it cometh not; And dig for it more than for hid treasures; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who rejoice unto exultation, And are glad, when they can find the grave?— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To a man whose way is hid, And whom God hath hedged in? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For my sighing cometh instead of my food, And my roarings are poured out like water. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the thing which I did fear is come upon me, And that which I was afraid of hath overtaken me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I was not at ease, neither was I quiet, Neither had I rest; but trouble came. <span class="anchor"
4: 4 Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If one venture a word unto thee, wilt thou be weary? But who can withhold himself from speaking? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Behold, thou hast instructed many, And thou hast strengthened the weak hands. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Thy words have upholden him that was falling, And thou hast strengthened the feeble knees. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But now it is come upon thee, and thou art weary;  ​ It toucheth thee, and thou art affrighted. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Is not thy fear of God thy confidence, And thy hope the integrity of thy ways? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
According as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, And sow mischief, reap the same. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
By the breath of God they perish, And by the blast of His anger are they consumed. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The lion roareth, and the fierce lion howleth— Yet the teeth of the young lions are broken. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, And the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Now a word was secretly brought to me, And mine ear received a whisper thereof. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
In thoughts from the visions of the night, When deep sleep falleth on men, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Fear came upon me, and trembling, And all my bones were made to shake. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then a spirit passed before my face, That made the hair of my flesh to stand up. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
It stood still, but I could not discern the appearance thereof; A form was before mine eyes; I heard a still voice: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Shall mortal man be just before God? Shall a man be pure before his Maker? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Behold, He putteth no trust in His servants, And His angels He chargeth with folly; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How much more them that dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Betwixt morning and evening they are shattered; They perish for ever without any regarding it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.' <span class="anchor"
5: 5 Call now; is there any that will answer thee? And to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For anger killeth the foolish man, And envy slayeth the silly one. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I have seen the foolish taking root; But suddenly I beheld his habitation cursed. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
His children are far from safety, And are crushed in the gate, with none to deliver them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, And taketh it even out of the thorns, and the snare gapeth for their substance. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For affliction cometh not forth from the dust, Neither doth trouble spring out of the ground; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But man is born unto trouble, As the sparks fly upward. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But as for me, I would seek unto God, And unto God would I commit my cause; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who doeth great things and unsearchable, Marvellous things without number; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who giveth rain upon the earth,  ​ And sendeth waters upon the fields; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So that He setteth up on high those that are low, And those that mourn are exalted to safety. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He frustrateth the devices of the crafty, So that their hands can perform nothing substantial. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He taketh the wise in their own craftiness; And the counsel of the wily is carried headlong. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
They meet with darkness in the day-time, And grope at noonday as in the night. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But He saveth from the sword of their mouth, Even the needy from the hand of the mighty. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So the poor hath hope, And iniquity stoppeth her mouth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth; Therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For He maketh sore, and bindeth up; He woundeth, and His hands make whole. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He will deliver thee in six troubles; Yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
In famine He will redeem thee from death; And in war from the power of the sword. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue; Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh; Neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field; And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace; And thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt miss nothing. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, And thine offspring as the grass of the earth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Thou shalt come to thy grave in a ripe age, Like as a shock of corn cometh in in its season. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lo this, we have searched it, So it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good. <span class="anchor"
6: 6 Then Job answered and said: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Oh that my vexation were but weighed, And my calamity laid in the balances altogether! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; t Herefore are my words broken. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up; The terrors of God do set themselves in array against me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Can that which hath no savour be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the juice of mallows? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My soul refuseth to touch them; They are as the sickness of my flesh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Oh that I might have my request, And that God would grant me the thing that I long for!  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Even that it would please God to crush me; That He would let loose His hand, and cut me off! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then should I yet have comfort; Yea, I would exult in pain, though He spare not; For I have not denied the words of the Holy One. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Is it that I have no help in me, And that sound wisdom is driven quite from me? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To him that is ready to faint kindness is due from his friend, Even to him that forsaketh the fear of the Almighty. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, As the channel of brooks that overflow, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Which are black by reason of the ice, And wherein the snow hideth itself; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
What time they wax warm, they vanish, When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The paths of their way do wind, They go up into the waste, and are lost. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The caravans of Tema looked, The companies of Sheba waited for them— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
They were ashamed because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For now ye are become His; Ye see a terror, and are afraid. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Did I say: 'Give unto me'? Or: 'Offer a present for me of your substance'? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
or: 'Deliver me from the adversary's hand'? Or: 'Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors'? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Teach me, and I will hold my peace; And cause me to understand wherein I have erred. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How forcible are words of uprightness! But what doth your arguing argue? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Do ye hold words to be an argument, But the speeches of one that is desperate to be wind? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Yea, ye would cast lots upon the fatherless, And dig a pit for your friend. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Now therefore be pleased to look upon me; For surely I shall not lie to your face. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice; Yea, return again, my cause is righteous. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern crafty devices? <span class="anchor"
7: 7 Is there not a time of service to man upon earth? And are not his days like the days of a hireling? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
As a servant that eagerly longeth for the shadow, And as a hireling that looketh for his wages; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So am I made to possess—months of vanity, And wearisome nights are appointed to me.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
When I lie down, I say: 'When shall I arise?' But the night is long, and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; My skin closeth up and breaketh out afresh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, And are spent without hope. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
O remember that my life is a breath; Mine eye shall no more see good. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more; While Thine eyes are upon me, I am gone. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, So he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He shall return no more to his house, Neither shall his place know him any more. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, That Thou settest a watch over me? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
When I say: 'My bed shall comfort me, My couch shall ease my complaint'; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then Thou scarest me with dreams, And terrifiest me through visions; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So that my soul chooseth strangling, And death rather than these my bones. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I loathe it; I shall not live alway; Let me alone; for my days are vanity. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
What is man, that Thou shouldest magnify him, And that Thou shouldest set Thy heart upon him, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And that Thou shouldest remember him every morning, And try him every moment? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How long wilt Thou not look away from me, Nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If I have sinned, what do I unto Thee, O Thou watcher of men? Why hast Thou set me as a mark for Thee, So that I am a burden to myself? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And why dost Thou not pardon my transgression, And take away mine iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust; And Thou wilt seek me, but I shall not be. <span class="anchor"
8: 8 Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How long wilt thou speak these things, Seeing that the words of thy mouth are as a mighty wind? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Doth God pervert judgment? Or doth the Almighty pervert justice? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If thy children sinned against Him, He delivered them into the hand of their transgression. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If thou wouldest seek earnestly unto God, And make thy supplication to the Almighty; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If thou wert pure and upright; Surely now He would awake for thee, And make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And though thy beginning was small, Yet thy end should greatly increase. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For inquire, I pray thee, of the former generation, And apply thyself to that which their fathers have searched out— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, Because our days upon earth are a shadow— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, And utter words out of their heart? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Can the rush shoot up without mire? Can the reed-grass grow without water? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Whilst it is yet in its greenness, and not cut down, It withereth before any other herb. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So are the paths of all that forget God; And the hope of the godless man shall perish; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Whose confidence is gossamer, And whose trust is a spider's web. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand; He shall hold fast thereby, but it shall not endure. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He is green before the sun, And his shoots go forth over his garden. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
His roots are wrapped about the heap, He beholdeth the place of stones. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If he be destroyed from his place, Then it shall deny him: 'I have not seen thee.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Behold, this is the joy of his way, And out of the earth shall others spring. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Behold, God will not cast away an innocent man, Neither will He uphold the evil-doers; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Till He fill thy mouth with laughter, And thy lips with shouting. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; And the tent of the wicked shall be no more. <span class="anchor"
9: 9 Then Job answered and said: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Of a truth I know that it is so; And how can man be just with God? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If one should desire to contend with Him, He could not answer Him one of a thousand. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength; Who hath hardened himself against Him, and prospered? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who removeth the mountains, and they know it not, When He overturneth them in His anger. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who shaketh the earth out of her place, And the pillars thereof tremble. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; And sealeth up the stars. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who alone stretcheth out the heavens, And treadeth upon the waves of the sea. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who doeth great things past finding out; Yea, marvellous things without number. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lo, He goeth by me, and I see Him not. He passeth on also, but I perceive Him not.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Behold, He snatcheth away, who can hinder Him? Who will say unto Him: 'What doest Thou?' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
God will not withdraw His anger; The helpers of Rahab did stoop under Him. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How much less shall I answer Him, And choose out my arguments with Him? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer; I would make supplication to Him that contendeth with me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If I had called, and He had answered me; Yet would I not believe that He would hearken unto my voice— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

He maketh a path to shine after him; One would think the deep to be hoary. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Upon earth there is not his like Who is made to be fearless. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He looketh at all high things; He is king over all the proud beasts. <span class="anchor"
42: 42 Then Job answered the Lord , and said: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I know that Thou canst do every thing, And that no purpose can be withholden from Thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who is this that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore have I uttered that which I understood not, Things too wonderful for me, which I knew not. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Hear, I beseech Thee, and I will speak; I will demand of Thee, and declare Thou unto me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I had heard of Thee by the hearing of the ear; But now mine eye seeth Thee; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Wherefore I abhor my words, and repent, Seeing I am dust and ashes. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

And it was so, that after the Lord had spoken these words unto Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite: 'My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends; for ye have not spoken of Me the thing that is right, as My servant Job hath. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Now therefore, take unto you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to My servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt-offering; and My servant Job shall pray for you; for him will I accept, that I do not unto you aught unseemly; for ye have not spoken of Me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the Lord commanded them; and the Lord accepted Job. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And the Lord changed the fortune of Job, when he prayed for his friends; and the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house; and they bemoaned him, and comforted him concerning all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him; every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one a ring of gold. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"

So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
He had also seven sons and three daughters. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And he called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
And after this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-default"
